title: Cross-Model Activation Generalizability Isn't Strong (Yet)
primary_claim: Cross-architecture activation similarity between small LLMs (1-3B, Llama/Gemma/Qwen/Pythia) is statistically significant (debiased CKA up to ~0.22, p<0.002 by permutation test) but weak, 4-9x lower than within-family similarity (up to 0.91), and linear bridges built on this cross-architecture structure transfer only coarse binary-classification signal and largely fail at next-token prediction, challenging the Platonic Representation Hypothesis at this scale.
metric: debiased CKA / linear-bridge probe transfer accuracy
target_value: cross-family max debiased CKA ~0.18-0.22 (mean 0.05-0.11) vs within-family max 0.914 (mean 0.605); within-family binary classification transfer reaches >90% of target-native accuracy at high rank, cross-family transfer plateaus below target-native and is inconsistent across tasks; cross-family next-token top-1 transfer caps at 4.9% vs within-family 93% of oracle

title: Introspection or entropy? Re-examining concept-injection “introspection” in open models
primary_claim: In open-weight models, concept-injection 'introspection' reports are better explained by injection-induced entropy that compresses the YES/NO logit gap toward zero (raising 'yes' rates even on unrelated factual questions) plus 'concept leakage' from the still-active steering vector, than by genuine introspective access: the introspection score averaged across 14 models is ~0 (mean +0.013, 95% CI [-0.1380, +0.1633], n.s.), and a concept-mismatch test finds no model with a statistically significant congruent-minus-incongruent detection gap.
metric: introspection score (delta-logit-detection minus delta-logit-factual), averaged across models
target_value: mean +0.013, median -0.032, 95% CI [-0.1380, +0.1633], n.s.; individual models range from +4.14 (Qwen-1.7B) to -2.83 (Qwen-32B)

title: GPT-2's IOI behavior is defined where the paper's algorithm isn't
primary_claim: In GPT-2 small's IOI circuit, incidentally duplicating the indirect-object name in an unrelated modifier slot causes Duplicate Token Heads to fire on it almost as strongly as on a genuine subject duplicate, yet this produces only a small drop in the IO/S logit difference (mean 0.23, Cohen's d=0.27) and accuracy barely changes (95.4% to 94.5%), because S-Inhibition heads mostly continue attending to the real S2 token rather than the incidental duplicate
metric: drop in IO/S logit difference between control and test (incidental duplicate) conditions; task accuracy
target_value: mean drop 0.23, SD 0.84 (n=128 matched pairs), paired t=3.09, p=0.0024, Cohen's d=0.27; accuracy 95.4% (control) vs 94.5% (test)

title: We need a better way to evaluate emergent misalignment
primary_claim: Standard emergent-misalignment evaluation prompts (as used by Betley et al.) substantially overestimate EM rates by misclassifying domain overfitting (e.g. a fiction-tuned model responding fictionally to serious questions) and in-domain misalignment as genuine broad/persona-level misalignment; using a judge prompt that discounts these non-emergent categories, real-world benign SFT datasets (finance, fiction) show only trace EM, and stylistic/formatting perturbations of hh-rlhf show no statistically significant EM signal
metric: EM rate (weighted average judge score) with original vs. adjusted evaluation prompt
target_value: adjusted prompt shows a significant delta (reduction) in EM rates across real-world SFT datasets and structured-output datasets vs. original prompt; e.g. fiction-finetune illegal-recommendation and finance-finetune medical-advice EM discounted; structured-output datasets show <10% above-baseline EM under adjusted prompt

title: Fork Around and Find Out Part 3: Interpreting the knight auditor
primary_claim: Layer-5 head-5 of the chess transformer Maia-3, previously identified as a 'knight fork detector,' is actually knight-move-specific (no effect on pawn forks) and functions as a 'knight move auditor' that scales support with the genuine threat value of a knight move and, most distinctively, harshly suppresses pointless (bad and quiet) knight moves nearly 3x more than bad attacking moves
metric: mean change in logit from ablating head l5h5, by move category
target_value: pawn K+Q fork +0.10 (unaffected); hollow attacks: queen +0.56, rook +0.13, bishop -0.01, pawn -0.11; good/bad x quiet/attacking: -0.30, -0.67, 0.78, 0.27 (pointless moves suppressed 2.93x harder than bad attacking moves)

title: Why Attack Success Rate Gives a False Picture of Backdoor Removal
primary_claim: The standard Attack Success Rate (ASR) metric drastically overstates the effectiveness of backdoor-removal techniques (attention-head ablation and 'backdoor vector' subtraction) from Backdoor Attribution (2025): using a richer output-quality metric (Good/Strange/Wrong/Refused) instead of exact-string matching, ablation success on Llama-2-7B-Chat drops from ~30% to ~1%, the backdoor-vector approach drops from 75% to 28% ASR-equivalent reduction on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and from 95% to 46% on Llama-2-7B-Chat, ASR also picks the wrong intervention layer, and ablation shows an 'alignment tax' degrading normal-input performance at or below the head-count needed to suppress the backdoor.
metric: Behavioral Attack Success Rate (BASR) vs original ASR reduction
target_value: backdoor vector: ASR reduction 75%->BASR 28% (Qwen2.5); 95%->46% (Llama-2); ablation: ASR-based 30% success -> new-metric ~1% success (Llama-2); best layer per ASR (layer 20) is worse than layer 11 by new metric (10x more good answers, >2x fewer refusals)

title: Features of SAEs are universal - but only up to an unknown random rotation
primary_claim: Independently trained sibling transformers compute the same function but their residual-stream activation bases differ by a rotation statistically indistinguishable from a uniform (Haar) draw on SO(d): applying one seed's SAE to another seed's activations catastrophically fails (negative explained variance) despite high (~0.9) decoder-column cosine similarity, while a single orthogonal Procrustes rotation restores reconstruction to 0.85-0.99 EV with no retraining.
target_value: 0.976-0.990 on toy model (vs worst-case -6.56 pre-rotation); 0.85-0.99 on Pythia-70m (vs -2.11 to 0.75 pre-rotation)

title: Does DiffusionGemma do latent reasoning?
primary_claim: DiffusionGemma's vector-valued latent state passed between diffusion steps is not essential for most reasoning tasks (top-k truncation performance loss found by Engels et al. is largely a sampler artifact fixable with a gentler sampler), interpretability techniques (probes, steering, J-lens) largely transfer from Gemma to DiffusionGemma, and while the model can use its distribution computationally in rare cases (e.g. letter arithmetic, parallel injections, palindrome generation), this remains interpretable superposition rather than opaque latent reasoning
metric: held-out AUC (probe transfer), blind judge accuracy (steering transfer), top-20 transfer fraction (J-lens transfer)
target_value: probes, steering, and J-lens largely transfer from Gemma to DiffusionGemma (specific numeric values in figures, not stated as single headline number in text)
